claim_one_line: THE FIRST PATCH SERIES OF THE ENFORCEMENT PACKAGE (WP-0.7), BUILT BY THE ADVISOR SEAT, VERIFIED WITH MAIN'S UNSEEN CASES AND LANDED: four patches under the rule that a gate is a function of the commit (a gate that needs git is refused where there is none; a gate that reads the past is refused on a shallow clone; a gate's day is the commit's and not the clock's; a commit dated before its parent is not trusted for its day). EIGHT OF MAIN'S NINE UNSEEN CASES HOLD: on an export with an empty .git directory all 20 gates of the table are refused, the five gates the seat's own list of ten did not name among them; with the five date variables set 400 days on and 30 days back, and with the system's date stubbed 400 days on, no gate of 53 changes its line; at depth 1, at depth 50 and on a full clone cut by a hand-written shallow file, all 14 gates that read the past are refused. ONE DOES NOT HOLD: a folder initialised as a repository with no commit is read as a full clone, and nine gates that have nothing to look at pass there; it is the seat's to close in a later series. Each patch's lock fails on the commit before it in the numbers the seat gave (7 of 7, 2, 4, 2); the series' lock passes (14) [CORRECTED 2026-11-12 (Review 79): no committed output showed that run; made again at Review 79's landing and committed, 14 passed]; main's 47 test files that name a gate pass once the views are generated; 53 gates pass. Not run: the whole suite on a fresh clone, and the seat's planted suite, whose 11 of 21 is the seat's count.
